name: Quick Add And Edit Dialogs
summary: Quick-add type and part dialogs, the Edit Part dialog, and supporting spec, quantity-type, image, and picker flows used from the active Dunnage workflow, including reusable quantity-type selection, conflict resolution between custom and saved quantity labels, definition-based part-specific specs for newly created parts, mixed payload reuse from existing part templates, and image previews that now resolve from the local Assets/DunnageImages cache first before falling back to the configured shared folder.

userActions: Add new types and parts quickly
Choose a saved quantity label header or enter a custom one when adding or editing a part
Resolve save-time conflicts when both a custom quantity type and a saved list value are provided
Optionally save a new custom quantity type for future reuse after a successful part save
Upload and clear PNG images for dunnage types and parts
See Dunnage image previews load from the local cache before falling back to the shared folder
See only the selected filename in the dunnage type image card instead of the full path
Click the selected dunnage type image preview to open its containing folder in File Explorer
See only the selected filename in the dunnage part image card instead of the full path
Click the selected dunnage part image preview to open its containing folder in File Explorer
Reuse an existing part's saved configured values, notes, and part-specific spec definitions when adding or editing a part
Define part-specific runtime spec fields for newly created parts when quick-adding or editing a part
Define a spec field with a controlled list of allowed choices
validationHints: Confirm type and part dialogs retain a selected PNG when reopened from draft state
Confirm Quick Add Part and Edit Part include a dedicated quantity-type step with a custom textbox and saved quantity-type list
Confirm leaving both quantity-type inputs blank saves the default label of Quantity
Confirm save-time conflict prompts let the user choose between the custom quantity type and the selected saved quantity type
Confirm canceling the conflict prompt returns the dialog to the quantity-type step when save was attempted from a different step
Confirm a saved part reopens with its current quantity type shown either in the saved list or the custom textbox, depending on where it came from
Confirm choosing to save a new custom quantity type inserts it into the reusable Dunnage quantity-type table after the part save succeeds
Confirm clearing an image removes the stored relative path on save
Confirm Quick Add Part and Edit Part can temporarily close, open the existing-spec picker, and reopen with the selected specs applied
Confirm choosing existing specs preserves mixed configured values plus part-specific spec-definition payloads without forcing the source part ID or inventory type
Confirm Quick Add Part saves configured type values plus part-specific spec definitions into one mixed JSON payload
Confirm Edit Part uses the new definition-based editor only for newly created parts that already carry part-specific spec definitions, while legacy parts stay on the key/value editor
Confirm part-specific spec definitions reject duplicate names and reserved keys that collide with configured specs or Notes
Confirm Quick Add Part and Edit Part render Choices specs as dropdowns using the configured array values
Confirm Quick Add Type shows the hidden choice editor only when the Choices spec type is selected
Confirm Dunnage image previews still render when the shared image folder is slow because the local cache copy exists
Confirm the Dunnage type image card shows only the selected filename and not the full source path
Confirm clicking the Dunnage type image preview opens File Explorer to the containing folder for the current image
Confirm the Dunnage part image card shows only the selected filename and not the full source path
Confirm clicking the Dunnage part image preview opens File Explorer to the containing folder for the current image
Confirm a type image chosen from the configured shared image root is persisted as Types/DunnageType-{TypeName}.{ext}
Confirm Edit Part no longer shows hardcoded width, height, or depth inputs and instead renders any dimension fields from the saved type spec definitions
Confirm all Dunnage Choose Image actions open in the configured shared image folder when that folder exists
Confirm deleting a type or part that is still referenced shows a plain-language blocking message instead of a raw database or foreign-key error
